name: open_distance
source: https://stopgettingscammed.vercel.app/indicators/vexel-plus/ (concept only: levels at set distances from the session open; formula is ours)
summary: +1 when the close first reaches a level a set fraction of the average daily range above the session open, -1 for the level below.

name: a158_cntd
source: Microsoft Qlib, Alpha158 factor set (github.com/microsoft/qlib, qlib/contrib/data/loader.py), factor CNTD
summary: +1 when up-closes outnumber down-closes over n bars by an unusual margin, -1 when down-closes do.

name: a158_cord
source: Microsoft Qlib, Alpha158 factor set (github.com/microsoft/qlib, qlib/contrib/data/loader.py), factor CORD
summary: +1 when up-bars have come with rising volume and down-bars with falling volume unusually often over n bars, -1 for the opposite.

name: a158_corr
source: Microsoft Qlib, Alpha158 factor set (github.com/microsoft/qlib, qlib/contrib/data/loader.py), factor CORR
summary: +1 when price and volume have risen and fallen together unusually closely over n bars, -1 when unusually oppositely.

name: a158_resi
source: Microsoft Qlib, Alpha158 factor set (github.com/microsoft/qlib, qlib/contrib/data/loader.py), factor RESI
summary: +1 when the close first stands unusually far above the line fitted to the last n closes, -1 when unusually far below.

name: a158_rsqr
source: Microsoft Qlib, Alpha158 factor set (github.com/microsoft/qlib, qlib/contrib/data/loader.py), factors RSQR and BETA
summary: +1 when the last n closes become unusually close to a straight rising line, -1 for a straight falling line.

name: a158_shadow
source: Microsoft Qlib, Alpha158 factor set (github.com/microsoft/qlib, qlib/contrib/data/loader.py), factors KUP and KLOW
summary: +1 when the lower shadow is unusually long against the last 500 bars, -1 when the upper shadow is.

name: a158_vsumd
source: Microsoft Qlib, Alpha158 factor set (github.com/microsoft/qlib, qlib/contrib/data/loader.py), factor VSUMD
summary: Volume has been building unusually strongly over n bars: +1 if price rose over those bars, -1 if it fell.

name: alpha007
source: Z. Kakushadze, "101 Formulaic Alphas" (2016), arXiv:1601.00991, Alpha#7
summary: Volume is above its 20-bar average and the 7-bar price change is among the largest of the last 60 bars: +1 if up, -1 if down.

name: alpha012
source: Z. Kakushadze, "101 Formulaic Alphas" (2016), arXiv:1601.00991, Alpha#12
summary: +1 after an unusually large fall on rising volume (or rise on falling volume), -1 after an unusually large rise on rising volume (or fall on falling volume).

name: alpha021
source: Z. Kakushadze, "101 Formulaic Alphas" (2016), arXiv:1601.00991, Alpha#21
summary: +1 when the 2-bar average close first drops below the 8-bar average minus one standard deviation, -1 when it first rises above the average plus one.

name: alpha023
source: Z. Kakushadze, "101 Formulaic Alphas" (2016), arXiv:1601.00991, Alpha#23
summary: -1 when the high is above its 20-bar average and has risen unusually fast over 2 bars; +1 for the mirror image on the lows.

name: alpha035
source: Z. Kakushadze, "101 Formulaic Alphas" (2016), arXiv:1601.00991, Alpha#35
summary: +1 when volume ranks high while price and the last return rank low against recent bars to an unusual degree; -1 for the mirror image.

name: alpha046
source: Z. Kakushadze, "101 Formulaic Alphas" (2016), arXiv:1601.00991, Alpha#46 (same quantity in Alpha#49 and Alpha#51)
summary: -1 when the last 10 bars rose unusually much faster than the 10 before, +1 when they fell unusually much faster.

name: alpha054
source: Z. Kakushadze, "101 Formulaic Alphas" (2016), arXiv:1601.00991, Alpha#54
summary: +1 when a bar closes unusually near its low (by the Alpha#54 score), -1 when unusually near its high.

name: cmf_extreme
source: freqtrade-strategies (github.com/freqtrade/freqtrade-strategies), berlinguyinca/TechnicalExampleStrategy (Chaikin Money Flow)
summary: +1 when volume-weighted closes have been unusually near the bar highs over n bars, -1 when unusually near the lows.

name: crabel_idnr
source: T. Crabel, "Day Trading with Short Term Price Patterns and Opening Range Breakout" (1990), ID/NR4 and NR7 patterns
summary: The previous bar sat inside the bar before it and had the narrowest range of n bars: +1 if this bar closes above its high, -1 if below its low.

name: high_volume_premium
source: Gervais, Kaniel and Mingelgrin, "The High-Volume Return Premium", Journal of Finance 56(3), 2001
summary: +1 when this bar's volume is in the top tenth of the same hour's volume over the last 50 days, -1 when it is in the bottom tenth.

name: intraday_momentum
source: Gao, Han, Li and Zhou, "Market Intraday Momentum", Journal of Financial Economics 129(2), 2018
summary: Late in the session, +1 if price rose from the previous close to the end of the session's first hour, -1 if it fell.

name: opening_range_break
source: T. Crabel, "Day Trading with Short Term Price Patterns and Opening Range Breakout" (1990); Zarattini and Aziz, "Can Day Trading Really Be Profitable?" (2023, SSRN)
summary: +1 at the first close above the high of the session's first hour, -1 at the first close below its low (same UTC day).

name: realized_skew
source: Amaya, Christoffersen, Jacobs and Vasquez, "Does Realized Skewness Predict the Cross-Section of Equity Returns?", Journal of Financial Economics 118(1), 2015
summary: +1 when the skewness of the last n hourly returns is unusually positive, -1 when unusually negative.

name: round_number_cross
source: C. Osler, "Currency Orders and Exchange Rate Dynamics: An Explanation for the Predictive Success of Technical Analysis", Journal of Finance 58(5), 2003
summary: +1 when the close moves up through a round number (a power-of-ten step sized to the market's own price), -1 when it moves down through one.

name: same_hour_seasonality
source: Heston, Korajczyk and Sadka, "Intraday Patterns in the Cross-Section of Stock Returns", Journal of Finance 65(4), 2010
summary: +1 when the clock hour that follows this bar rose on each of the last k days, -1 when it fell on each of them.

name: smash_day
source: L. Williams, "Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading" (1999), smash day reversals
summary: +1 when the previous bar closed below the low of the bar before it and this bar closes above the previous bar's high; -1 for the mirror image.

name: td_setup
source: freqtrade-strategies (github.com/freqtrade/freqtrade-strategies), berlinguyinca/TDSequentialStrategy; count from T. DeMark, "The New Science of Technical Analysis" (1994)
summary: +1 when nine closes in a row are each below the close four bars earlier, -1 when nine in a row are each above it.

name: turn_of_month
source: Lakonishok and Smidt, "Are Seasonal Anomalies Real? A Ninety-Year Perspective", Review of Financial Studies 1(4), 1988; McConnell and Xu, "Equity Returns at the Turn of the Month", Financial Analysts Journal 64(2), 2008
summary: +1 at a fixed UTC hour on the last calendar day of a month and on days 1 to 3 of the next.

name: alpha008
source: Z. Kakushadze, "101 Formulaic Alphas" (2016), arXiv:1601.00991, Alpha#8
summary: -1 when the 5-bar return, weighted by price, has risen unusually much against its value 10 bars ago; +1 when it has fallen unusually much.

name: amihud_illiq
source: Y. Amihud, "Illiquidity and Stock Returns: Cross-Section and Time-Series Effects", Journal of Financial Markets 5(1), 2002
summary: +1 when price has been moving unusually far per unit of volume over n bars, -1 when unusually little.

name: cl_morning_star
source: Caginalp and Laurent, "The Predictive Power of Price Patterns", Applied Mathematical Finance 5 (1998), 181-205 (Morning Star / Evening Star)
summary: +1 when, after a downtrend, a down bar is followed by a bar that opens and closes below its close and then an up bar closing above the middle of the first bar's body; -1 for the mirror image after an uptrend.

name: cl_three_inside
source: Caginalp and Laurent, "The Predictive Power of Price Patterns", Applied Mathematical Finance 5 (1998), 181-205 (Three Inside Up / Three Inside Down)
summary: +1 when, after a downtrend, a down bar is followed by a bar whose body sits inside it and then an up bar closing above the first bar's open; -1 for the mirror image after an uptrend.

name: cl_three_outside
source: Caginalp and Laurent, "The Predictive Power of Price Patterns", Applied Mathematical Finance 5 (1998), 181-205 (Three Outside Up / Three Outside Down)
summary: +1 when, after a downtrend, a down bar is swallowed by an up bar and the next bar is an up bar closing higher still; -1 for the mirror image after an uptrend.

name: cl_three_soldiers
source: Caginalp and Laurent, "The Predictive Power of Price Patterns", Applied Mathematical Finance 5 (1998), 181-205 (Three White Soldiers / Three Black Crows)
summary: +1 when, after a downtrend, three up bars in a row each open inside the previous body and close higher; -1 for three down bars after an uptrend.

name: hikkake
source: D. Chesler, "Trading False Moves with the Hikkake Pattern", Active Trader (2004); summary at en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hikkake_pattern
summary: +1 at the first close above an inside bar's high within three bars of a false break below it, -1 for the mirror image.

name: serial_corr
source: B. LeBaron, "Some Relations Between Volatility and Serial Correlations in Stock Market Returns", Journal of Business 65(2), 1992
summary: When hourly returns have been unusually self-following over n bars, point with the last bar; when unusually self-reversing, point against it.

name: alexander_filter
source: Alexander, "Price Movements in Speculative Markets: Trends or Random Walks", Industrial Management Review 2(2), 1961; Fama and Blume, "Filter Rules and Stock-Market Trading", Journal of Business 39(1), 1966
summary: +1 when the close has risen k average true ranges above its low since the last down signal; -1 when it has fallen k average true ranges below its high since the last up signal.

name: alpha052
source: Z. Kakushadze, "101 Formulaic Alphas" (2016), arXiv:1601.00991, Alpha#52
summary: +1 when the 5-bar low has fallen unusually far on high volume after a strong longer-run return; -1 when it has risen unusually far under the same weights.

name: bvc_imbalance
source: Easley, Lopez de Prado and O'Hara, "Flow Toxicity and Liquidity in a High-frequency World", Review of Financial Studies 25(5), 2012, 1457-1493 (bulk volume classification)
summary: +1 when estimated buying, as a share of volume over the last 50 bars, first becomes unusually high for this market; -1 when estimated selling does.

name: fair_value_gap
source: NinjaTrader, "The Ultimate Guide to Trading Fair Value Gaps", ninjatrader.com/futures/blogs/fair-value-gaps (2026); see also Taylor, arXiv:2610.35887
summary: +1 when a bar's low is above the high of the bar two bars back by at least k average ranges; -1 when its high is below that bar's low by as much.

name: lmw_broadening
source: Lo, Mamaysky and Wang, "Foundations of Technical Analysis: Computational Algorithms, Statistical Inference, and Empirical Implementation", Journal of Finance 55(4), 2000, 1705-1765 (Broadening top and bottom)
summary: -1 when five turning points starting with a high make higher highs and lower lows; +1 when five starting with a low make lower lows and higher highs.

name: lmw_double
source: Lo, Mamaysky and Wang, "Foundations of Technical Analysis: Computational Algorithms, Statistical Inference, and Empirical Implementation", Journal of Finance 55(4), 2000, 1705-1765 (Double top and double bottom)
summary: -1 when a new high matches an earlier high 23 to 35 bars back with no higher high between them; +1 for two matching lows.

name: lmw_head_shoulders
source: Lo, Mamaysky and Wang, "Foundations of Technical Analysis: Computational Algorithms, Statistical Inference, and Empirical Implementation", Journal of Finance 55(4), 2000, 1705-1765 (Head-and-shoulders and inverse head-and-shoulders)
summary: -1 when five turning points form a head-and-shoulders top (middle high above two near-equal shoulders, near-equal lows between); +1 for the mirror image.

name: lmw_rectangle
source: Lo, Mamaysky and Wang, "Foundations of Technical Analysis: Computational Algorithms, Statistical Inference, and Empirical Implementation", Journal of Finance 55(4), 2000, 1705-1765 (Rectangle top and bottom)
summary: -1 when five turning points starting with a high have near-equal highs and near-equal lows; +1 when the five start with a low.

name: lmw_triangle
source: Lo, Mamaysky and Wang, "Foundations of Technical Analysis: Computational Algorithms, Statistical Inference, and Empirical Implementation", Journal of Finance 55(4), 2000, 1705-1765 (Triangle top and bottom)
summary: -1 when five turning points starting with a high make lower highs and higher lows; +1 when five starting with a low make higher lows and lower highs.

name: opex_week
source: Stivers and Sun, "Returns and option activity over the option-expiration week for S&P 100 stocks", Journal of Banking & Finance 37(11), 2013, 4226-4240
summary: +1 at a fixed UTC hour on the Monday of the week that holds the month's third Friday.

name: dow_swing
source: W. P. Hamilton, "The Stock Market Barometer" (1922); R. Rhea, "The Dow Theory" (1932); Brown, Goetzmann and Kumar, "The Dow Theory: William Peter Hamilton's Track Record Reconsidered", Journal of Finance 53(4), 1998
summary: +1 when the close moves above the last swing high after a swing low that was higher than the one before; -1 when it moves below the last swing low after a lower swing high.

name: osler_hs_neckline
source: C. L. Osler, "Identifying Noise Traders: The Head-and-Shoulders Pattern in U.S. Equities", Federal Reserve Bank of New York Staff Report 42, 1998
summary: -1 on the first close below the line through the two troughs of a three-peak pattern whose middle peak is highest; +1 for the mirror image.

name: three_line_break
source: S. Nison, "Beyond Candlesticks: New Japanese Charting Techniques Revealed", Wiley, 1994 (three-line break charts)
summary: +1 when, during a run of falling lines, the close rises above the highest point of the last three lines; -1 when, during a run of rising lines, it falls below their lowest point.

name: supertrend_flip
source: SuperTrend indicator (credited to Olivier Seban), standard public definition; link supplied by Jeff: tradingview.com/script/4UaDaKOX-SuperTrend (not opened)
summary: +1 when the close moves above the trailing upper band (bar midpoint plus 3 average true ranges, only allowed to fall); -1 when it moves below the trailing lower band.

name: supercycle_surge
source: DaviddTech, "SuperCycle Surge Strategy" (invite-only TradingView script; public description only, settings withheld); parts: Ehlers 2013 Super Smoother, Schaff Trend Cycle, Dreiss Choppiness Index, at their customary defaults
summary: +1 on the first bar where the close is above the Super Smoother, the Schaff Trend Cycle is rising and the Choppiness Index is below its line; -1 for the mirror image.

name: trendilo_turn
source: Trendilo, open-source TradingView indicator (public description via web search, page not opened; defaults from recall); the base of DaviddTech's invite-only "Trendhoo" strategy, whose own rules are not public
summary: +1 when the smoothed percent change of the close rises above its own root-mean-square band; -1 when it falls below the band on the other side.

name: gtja160_down_vol
source: Guotai Junan Securities, 191 short-horizon price-volume alpha factors (2017), Alpha#160, as documented at https://shrektan.github.io/techfactor
summary: -1 when volatility on non-rising bars (Alpha#160) first reaches a high extreme of its own past, +1 when it first reaches a low extreme.

name: lagged_session_sign
source: Wu and Pinsky, "On the Performance of Lagged Momentum and Reversal Strategies Across Daytime and Overnight Sessions in Bitcoin and Ethereum Cryptocurrencies", J. Risk Financial Manag. 19(9), 692, 2026, https://www.mdpi.com/1911-8074/19/9/692
summary: At the bar that closes at hour h UTC: +1 if the 12 hours starting at h rose a day earlier, -1 if they fell.

name: obv_divergence
source: J. Granville, "Granville's New Key to Stock Market Profits", 1963 (on-balance volume non-confirmation)
summary: -1 when the close makes a new n-bar high but on-balance volume does not, +1 when the close makes a new n-bar low but on-balance volume does not.

name: tweezer
source: S. Nison, "Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques", 1991; Marshall, Young and Rose, Journal of Banking and Finance 30(8), 2006
summary: -1 when an up bar and then a down bar share the same high at an n-bar high, +1 when a down bar and then an up bar share the same low at an n-bar low.

name: gtja003_pressure_sum
source: Guotai Junan Securities, 191 short-horizon price-volume alpha factors (2017), Alpha#3 and Alpha#59, as listed at https://bigquant.com/wiki/doc/Pyf0TYya6H
summary: +1 when the n-bar sum of close-minus-true-low (up bars) and close-minus-true-high (down bars) first reaches a high extreme of its own past, -1 at a low extreme.

name: gtja009_ease_of_movement
source: Guotai Junan Securities, 191 short-horizon price-volume alpha factors (2017), Alpha#9 and Alpha#68, as listed at https://bigquant.com/wiki/doc/Pyf0TYya6H
summary: +1 when smoothed ease of movement (midpoint move x range / volume) first reaches a high extreme of its own past, -1 at a low extreme.

name: gtja118_open_reach
source: Guotai Junan Securities, 191 short-horizon price-volume alpha factors (2017), Alpha#118, as listed at https://bigquant.com/wiki/doc/Pyf0TYya6H
summary: +1 when the 20-bar ratio of (high - open) to (open - low) first reaches a high extreme of its own past, -1 at a low extreme.

name: lunar_phase
source: Dichev and Janes, "Lunar Cycle Effects in Stock Returns", Journal of Private Equity 6(4), 2003; Yuan, Zheng and Zhu, "Are Investors Moonstruck? Lunar Phases and Stock Returns", Journal of Empirical Finance 13(1), 2006
summary: +1 on the first bar at or after each new moon, -1 on the first bar at or after each full moon (mean lunar cycle).

name: td_differential
source: Thomas DeMark, New Market Timing Techniques (Wiley, 1997), TD Differential and TD Reverse Differential, as described at https://www.litefinance.org/blog/for-professionals/a-set-of-differential-tools-by-thomas-demark-td-differential-td-anti-differential-td-reverse-differential/
summary: reverse=0: +1 after two lower closes with buying pressure rising and selling pressure falling, -1 for the mirror. reverse=1: the continuation version, with the pressure conditions swapped.

name: vsa_no_demand
source: Tom Williams, Master the Markets (TradeGuider), no-demand and no-supply bars, as described at https://www.luxalgo.com/library/concept/no-demand-no-supply-bars/ and https://therighttrader.com/learn/volume-and-order-flow/no-demand-bar
summary: -1 on an up-close bar with a narrow range and volume below each of the two bars before it (no demand); +1 on the down-close mirror (no supply).

name: acceleration
source: D. Ardila-Alvarez, Z. Forro and D. Sornette, "The acceleration effect and Gamma factor in asset pricing", Physica A 569, 125367 (2021), https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/phsmap/v569y2021ics0378437120307196.html
summary: +1 when the last n bars' return minus the n bars' return before it first rises 2 standard deviations above its own recent average; -1 when it first falls 2 below.

name: friday_monday_sign
source: F. Cross, "The Behavior of Stock Prices on Fridays and Mondays", Financial Analysts Journal 29(6), 1973; A. Abraham and D. Ikenberry, "The Individual Investor and the Weekend Effect", JFQA 29(2), 1994
summary: On the Monday bar that starts at `hour` UTC: +1 if Friday rose (20:00 UTC Thursday to 20:00 UTC Friday), -1 if it fell.

name: td_camouflage
source: T. DeMark, "The New Science of Technical Analysis" (1994); J. Perl, "DeMark Indicators" (2008); rule read at wickra-docs.pages.dev/Indicators/Indicator-TdCamouflage
summary: +1 when the close is below the previous close but above the open and the low is under the previous low; -1 for the mirror image.

name: td_clop
source: J. Perl, "DeMark Indicators" (2008), TD Clop, after T. DeMark; rule read at wickra-docs.pages.dev/Indicators/Indicator-TdClop
summary: +1 when the bar opens below the previous bar's open and close and closes above both; -1 for the mirror image.

name: td_clopwin
source: J. Perl, "DeMark Indicators" (2008), TD Clopwin, after T. DeMark; rule read at wickra-docs.pages.dev/Indicators/Indicator-TdClopwin
summary: The bar's open and close are both inside the previous bar's body: +1 if it closes above its open, -1 if below.

name: td_countdown
source: T. DeMark, "The New Science of Technical Analysis" (1994), TD Sequential countdown; J. Perl, "DeMark Indicators" (2008)
summary: +1 at the 13th close at or below the low two bars earlier after nine closes in a row below the close four bars earlier; -1 for the mirror image.

name: td_line_break
source: T. DeMark, "The New Science of Technical Analysis" (1994), TD Points and TD Lines
summary: +1 when the close crosses above the falling line through the last two swing highs, -1 when it crosses below the rising line through the last two swing lows.

name: turnaround_tuesday
source: L. Williams, "Turnaround Tuesday"; rule read in "Turnaround Tuesday: The One-Day Edge That Still Works", Alpha Algo Trading Research, https://algotr.substack.com/p/turnaround-tuesday-the-one-day-edge (2026)
summary: On the Monday bar that starts at `hour` UTC: +1 if its close is above the close at the same hour on Friday, -1 if below.

name: advance_block
source: TA-Lib, CDLADVANCEBLOCK, https://ta-lib.org/functions/cdladvanceblock.html; pattern from S. Nison, Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques, 1991
summary: -1 when three up bars with rising closes have shrinking bodies and a growing upper shadow; +1 for three down bars with shrinking bodies and a growing lower shadow.

name: cooper_volume_filter
source: M. Cooper, Filter Rules Based on Price and Volume in Individual Security Overreaction, Review of Financial Studies 12(4), 1999
summary: +1 after a large n-bar rise and -1 after a large n-bar fall, kept only when volume over those n bars was lower (falling=1) or higher (falling=0) than over the n bars before.

name: three_line_strike
source: TA-Lib, CDL3LINESTRIKE, https://ta-lib.org/functions/cdl3linestrike.html
summary: +1 when three up bars with rising closes are followed by a down bar that closes below the first bar's open; -1 for three down bars and an up bar closing above the first bar's open.

name: three_methods
source: TA-Lib, CDLRISEFALL3METHODS, https://ta-lib.org/functions/cdlrisefall3methods.html; pattern from S. Nison, Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques, 1991
summary: +1 when a long up bar, three small down bars inside its range and a long up bar closing above the first follow one another; -1 for the mirror image.

name: month_end_reversal
source: Etula, Rinne, Suominen and Vaittinen, "Dash for Cash: Monthly Market Impact of Institutional Liquidity Needs", Review of Financial Studies 33(1), 2020, https://doi.org/10.1093/rfs/hhz054
summary: At 00:00 UTC on the fourth-last weekday of a month: +1 if the five weekdays before it fell, -1 if they rose (leg 1). At 00:00 UTC on the fourth weekday of a month: +1 if the four weekdays before it fell, -1 if they rose (leg 2).

name: same_weekday_sign
source: Z. Da and X. Zhang, "Same-Weekday Momentum", working paper, 2025, https://papers.ssrn.com/abstract=4806275; Keloharju, Linnainmaa and Nyberg, "Return Seasonalities", Journal of Finance 71(4), 2016
summary: Once a day at `hour` UTC: +1 if the 24 hours from this hour rose on average on the same weekday 5 to 52 weeks ago, -1 if they fell on average.

name: noise_band_break
source: Zarattini, Aziz and Barbon, "Beat the Market: An Effective Intraday Momentum Strategy for S&P500 ETF (SPY)", 2024, SSRN 4824172, https://alexandria.unisg.ch/server/api/core/bitstreams/a99aba00-f967-49b3-aceb-f544dc386e0b/content
summary: +1 when the close first rises above the day's open (or previous close, if higher) by more than the average move from the open at this hour over the last 14 days; -1 for the mirror below.
